newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest direct hogs seen off $0.50-$1-dealers.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest direct hogs seen off $0.50-$1-dealers.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct cash hogs Wednesday were seen $0.50 to $1.00 per cwt lower, pressured by outlooks for increased hog movement, livestock dealers said.
Road conditions were expected to improve Wednesday, which will allow producers to more easily sort and ship hogs. Blowing snow curbed hog runs Tuesday in the western Corn Belt.

Iowa and southern Minnesota top prices for hogs delivered to plants could range from $53.50 to $54.50, sources there said. Illinois top prices at plants could range from $53.00 to $54.00 while Indiana/Ohio top plant prices were seen at $53.00 to $54.00, cash dealers and packer buyers in those areas said.
Snowfall amounnts of 12 inches or more were reported by hog buyers and dealers in eastern South Dakota, southern Minnesota and western and northern Iowa.

Several plant operations in the area not only had trouble getting hogs, but also had difficulty getting enough employees to show up for second shifts, especially plants dependent on workers who had to drive in from rural areas, cash market sources said.
Tuesday's slaughter was estimated by USDA at 315,000 head, below 338,000 a week ago and 351,000 a year ago.
